# Research notes (Stage 1) — verified 2026-11-17

## Markets
* All seven assets have live 5-minute UP/DOWN markets. Slugs follow `{btc|eth|sol|xrp|doge|hype|bnb}-updown-5m-{unix_start}`,
  windows are aligned to 300 s, and each event holds one binary market (`outcomes = ["Up","Down"]`, `clobTokenIds` [UP, DOWN]).
* Rules: *"resolve to Up if the time-weighted average price (TWAP) of [asset], generated by Chainlink, of the time range … is
  greater than or equal to the price at the beginning of that range."* `cryptoMarketConfig = {id: "btc-5m-twap-60",
  twapEnabled: true, twapLookbackSeconds: 60}`; resolution source `data.chain.link/streams/btc-usd-twap-60s-streams`.
  Ties resolve **UP**.
* Opening reference = `polymarket.com/api/crypto/crypto-price … openPrice`. It equals the previous window's `closePrice`.
* Official resolution: Gamma `closed=true`, `umaResolutionStatus="resolved"`, `outcomePrices` ["1","0"] / ["0","1"],
  about 80 s after window end (`automaticallyResolved: true`).
* Market flags: `restricted: true`, `orderMinSize: 5`, `orderPriceMinTickSize: 0.01` (tick can change near the extremes via
  `tick_size_change`), `negRisk: false`.

## Fees (docs.polymarket.com/trading/fees)
* `fee = C × feeRate × p × (1 − p)`, in USDC, taker only. Crypto: rate 0.07 (`feeType: crypto_fees_v2`, `exponent: 1`),
  maker fee 0, maker rebate 20 %. Fees are rounded to 5 dp, with a minimum of 0.00001.
* Example: buying 100 shares at $0.03 costs $3.00 + $0.2037 fee, so the break-even win rate is 3.204 %.
* The CLOB `/fee-rate` endpoint reports `base_fee: 1000` (bps). The authoritative curve is the market's `feeSchedule`.

## Free public access (no key)
| API | Auth | Limits (docs) |
|---|---|---|
| Gamma `gamma-api.polymarket.com` | none | /events 500 req/10 s, /markets 300/10 s |
| CLOB REST `/book`, `/prices-history` | none | /book 1500/10 s, /books 500/10 s |
| CLOB WS market channel | none | PING every 10 s; 100-token cap removed 2025-05-28 |
| RTDS `ws-live-data.polymarket.com` (`crypto_prices_chainlink`) | none | undocumented; one socket carries all symbols |
| crypto-price (web endpoint) | none | undocumented, so polled conservatively |
| Binance public streams | none | 5 msg/s inbound, 1024 streams/connection |
| Data API | v1 **retired**; v2 exists | not needed for paper trading |
| CLOB trading | L1 EIP-712 + L2 HMAC | per-signer buckets; **not used (NL restricted)** |

Geographic: `polymarket.com/api/geoblock` returns `{"blocked": true, "country": "NL"}` from this machine. Public data reads
work; order placement is prohibited. The app does not circumvent this.

## Historical data
* There is no public historical order-book depth.
* `prices-history` gives about 1-minute price points per token. That supports coarse calibration only (≈T-60/T-120).
* Gamma serves every past window's official outcome, so historical win/loss labels are reliable.

## Research context
* Prediction-market prices are often well calibrated in aggregate, but long-shot / favourite-longshot bias is widely
  documented in betting and prediction markets: very cheap contracts tend to win *less* often than their price implies.
  If that holds here, buying 1–3 c underdogs is negative EV before fees, and the fee (≈7 % × p) makes it worse.
  The application is built to measure this, not to assume it.
* The 60 s TWAP settlement is crucial. At T-10 about 50 s of the averaging window is already fixed, so a late spot move must
  be large to flip the outcome. Expect reversal frequencies at T-5…T-1 to be **lower** than spot-only intuition suggests.
* Executable cost ≠ midpoint: the underdog's ask at 1–2 c often has thin size. That is why the scanner reports book-walk
  prices for a $10 order and flags thin-liquidity opportunities separately.
